You are doing a READ-ONLY Jira sweep for the Zimmermann SFCC project (Atlassian site: zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net, project key SFCC). Use the mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_* tools. Load them via ToolSearch first: query "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue,mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search".

DO NOT WRITE ANYTHING TO JIRA. No comments, no transitions, no field edits. Read only.

GOAL: Find everything in Jira relating to Salesforce EINSTEIN / CQuotient / Recommendations, specifically as it bears on two stories the user is building right now: SFCC-83 "Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared)" and SFCC-84 "Recently Viewed - See Full History".

Tasks:

1. Read these specific issues in full (summary, description, status, assignee, labels, sprint, ALL comments, links, parent epic):
   - SFCC-112 (Recommendations – Einstein Configuration & Zone Setup)
   - SFCC-7 (Search & Recommendations epic)
   - SFCC-118 (carousel UI)
   - SFCC-642 (Einstein AI Sort BM config)
   - SFCC-647
   - SFCC-106 (consent gating for tracking)
   - SFCC-236 (product card shared component — for context on the card used in the rail)
   Report the CURRENT status of each (they may have moved since 2026-08-10).

2. Run JQL searches to find anything else Einstein/recommendations-related. Suggested queries (run several, vary them):
   - project = SFCC AND (summary ~ "Einstein" OR description ~ "Einstein")
   - project = SFCC AND (summary ~ "recommendation" OR description ~ "recommendation")
   - project = SFCC AND (summary ~ "CQuotient" OR description ~ "CQuotient")
   - project = SFCC AND (summary ~ "recently viewed" OR description ~ "recently viewed")
   - project = SFCC AND text ~ "viewProduct"
   - project = SFCC AND text ~ "zone"
   Report every distinct issue found with key, summary, status, assignee, sprint, and a one-line note on why it is relevant.

3. For SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 specifically: retrieve their issue LINKS and parent epic, and check whether any Einstein issue is linked as a blocker/dependency. Also check whether SFCC-83/84 have acceptance criteria in a custom field (try fields="*all" and look for AC / Acceptance Criteria custom fields, and for a DoR checklist).

4. Critically: determine whether ANY Jira ticket states where Recently Viewed browsing history is SUPPOSED to be stored for authenticated shoppers — Einstein/CQuotient user profile, an SFCC customer custom attribute, localStorage, or something else. Quote the exact text and the ticket it comes from. If no ticket says, say so explicitly — that is a finding.

RETURN FORMAT:
- A table of every Einstein-related issue: key | summary | status | assignee | sprint | relevance to SFCC-83/84
- The exact current status of SFCC-112 (this is the gating one)
- Any explicit statement about Recently Viewed storage/persistence mechanism, quoted verbatim with its source ticket
- Anything you could NOT read (permission error, missing ticket) — name it explicitly
Be precise and quote rather than paraphrase where it matters. Do not speculate; if something is absent, say it is absent.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. - zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.

- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).

- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.

However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. - anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.

- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

## Storage / persistence — what Jira actually says

The only verbatim statements, both from **SFCC-83** (description and Acceptance Criteria field `customfield_10231`):

> "For **guest shoppers*: history is stored temporarily. It persists for the duration of that session only."
> "For **authenticated shoppers*: history persisted cross-session — stored against the customer account so it survives browser close and is available on login from any device."

AC 7: *"Given an authenticated shopper has previously viewed products, when they log in on any device, then their Recently Viewed history is restored and displayed in the rail."*

**No ticket anywhere in the project names the mechanism.** "Stored against the customer account" is the furthest any ticket goes — it does not say Einstein/CQuotient profile, SFCC customer custom attribute, Omneo, or localStorage. Confirmed absent, not merely unfound:

The nearest contrast is **SFCC-118** AC 7, which *does* name a mechanism — but for Recommended for You, not Recently Viewed: *"Given a shopper is logged in... then recommendations are driven by their browsing and purchase history via Einstein Product Recommendations."*

For guests, **SFCC-106** is the firmest statement: *"products viewed during that session are shown. When the browser session ends, the history is cleared."*

1. **Scope contradiction.** SFCC-7 (your parent epic) lists in scope: *"'Recently Viewed' on PDP, PLP and cart"* — inside a Recommendations bullet, in an epic premised on being *"powered by Salesforce Einstein natively within the platform."* Yet SFCC-112 provisions no Recently Viewed zone and no Einstein ticket links to SFCC-83/84. 3. **Consent wording was stripped mid-edit.** SFCC-83 AC 6 reads *"Given a guest shopper{color:#ff5630} {color}browses products"* — a leftover colour marker where "has given consent" was removed (per Jasmijn's 2026-07-14 comment moving consent to SFCC-106). SFCC-106 retains both the consent and no-consent variants, and is **Blocked** pending the Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley review. SFCC-106 also notes: *"the current Magento behaviour for some components (e.g. Recently Viewed) does not consent-gate correctly."*
